name: HTTP Client
description: Organize saved HTTP requests, switch environments, import cURL and inspect responses
help: Requests are sent by the local Rust engine as a cancellable task; nothing goes through a third-party service.
JSON responses are pretty-printed; large bodies show a preview and can be saved in full.
Addresses without a scheme use https, or http for localhost and private networks. Localhost always bypasses the system proxy.
Copy as cURL turns the current request into a shell command.
Saved requests and environments are stored locally. Secret variable values last only for this session.

The Auth tab supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE: sign in through the system browser and receive the callback on 127.0.0.1. Tokens live only in memory for this run and are isolated per environment.

Turn on “Stream” next to the address bar to show the response as it arrives: text/event-stream is parsed into SSE event, id, data and retry fields, other chunked responses are shown chunk by chunk. Search, stop, export and resume with Last-Event-ID. Streaming has no timeout, does not follow redirects or use the system proxy, and keeps the latest 5000 items.
Use Ctrl / Command + Enter to send the current request.
